newsitem.title: UK: Air Canada to levy no-show cargo penalties.
newsitem.headline: Air Canada to levy no-show cargo penalties.

text.p: Air Canada will apply no-show penalties from March 1 on forwarders and shippers in Europe who book consignments on weekend flights but then do not deliver, the airline's manager-cargo Europe, Des Vertannes said
The penalities will apply when insufficient notice of non-delivery is given, he said.
In a letter to customers, he said the charge would be 50 percent of booked weight at the applicable tariff.

"The no-show shipment is still a regular occurrence and in certain (European) markets accounts for an average of 16 to 19 percent of total bookings. Although efforts to monitor, identify and take appropriate action have shown some success, it is obvious that more penetrating and dramatic action is needed," states the letter.
It adds many Air Canada cargo customers are restricted from obtaining weekend capacity on the airline due to this no-show factor.

"This move has not been made in an attempt to obtain extra revenue and the levy will only be imposed on people who book space with Air Canada and then don't send us a single kilo, perhaps because they get a better last minute offer from elsewhere," Vertannes told Reuters.
"This is a matter of common courtesy. No-shows are unacceptable in this day and age," he said. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706; fax +5017
